head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's.
reason: EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents (lines 845-870) loads the organizer's credential from the database by `reference.credentialId` when the caller doesn't hold it, and wraps the work in try/catch, so the caller's credentials don't block the update and the request doesn't error.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, so they can be bypassed.
reason: Lines 71-77 lowercase the blacklist but compare the raw `guest` with `includes` and `===`, and the schema `z.array(z.string().email())` doesn't remove duplicates, so mixed-case and repeated emails get through.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Emails use the raw `guests` list instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`.
reason: sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:541) sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to everyone in `newGuests`, and the handler passes the unfiltered `guests`, so an existing attendee included in the request gets a new 'scheduled' email.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected or past bookings.
reason: The handler checks only that the booking exists and that the user has permission (lines 44-56); it never checks booking status or end time before writing attendees and sending invites.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Team admin/owner check uses && so only owners get through.
reason: isTeamAdmin already matches both ADMIN and OWNER while isTeamOwner matches OWNER only, so `&&` lets only owners through and a plain ADMIN gets FORBIDDEN.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: A calendar update failure after the DB write leaves a half-done state, and retrying fails.
reason: updateCalendarAttendees returns early when there are no references, and updateAllCalendarEvents catches errors and returns failure results instead of throwing, so the half-finished, unretryable state described doesn't arise from it.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: No cap on the number of guests, and any attendee can add them, so this can be abused to send email spam.
reason: The schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max, any attendee passes the permission check, and each new guest gets a platform-sent invitation email, so this can be used to send mass email.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: The fallback error message can never show, and the error banner is never cleared on success.
reason: The template string at line 43 is never empty, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is dead code, and `isInvalidEmail` is reset only in the Cancel handler, not in onSuccess.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Crash when the location is Google Meet and there is no destination calendar.
reason: Line 118-119: `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` leaves mainHostDestinationCalendar undefined and `.integration` is read without optional chaining, throwing for Meet locations.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The organization slug condition is inverted, which is unrelated to this PR.
reason: The diff flips `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, so the slug is set with billing on and missing with billing off; this is unrelated to the PR.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: deleteEvent fallback can never match and always falls through to "primary".
reason: Lines 315-317: the find runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy and compares against that falsy value, so it never matches and deletes fall to 'primary' instead of the old destinationCalendar.externalId.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Video references lose their credentialId.
reason: Line 170 sets credentialId undefined for non-calendar results, and handleCancelBooking.ts:491 relies on `bookingVideoReference.credentialId`.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Collective hosts' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar.
reason: destinationCalendar becomes null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op and the other hosts' calendars are lost.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: A destination calendar without a credentialId now writes to "primary" instead of its externalId.
reason: CalendarManager.createEvent passes credential.id and Google selects the calendar only by matching credentialId, so destination rows without a credentialId go to 'primary' instead of their externalId.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Office365 (and similarly Lark/CalDAV) use the main host's calendar id with every host's credential.
reason: Office365 createEvent always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId, while createAllCalendarEvents now calls it once per host destination with that host's credential.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId.
reason: CalendarManager.updateEvent's return value has no externalId, so `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` in updateLocation (line 208) is always undefined, where before it came from evt.destinationCalendar.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: References for legacy destinations without a credentialId get no externalCalendarId.
reason: Line 380 calls createEvent(c, event) without an externalId, and CalendarManager.createEvent returns the passed externalId, so these references store undefined.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Recurring cancellation repeats once per reference and still deletes only the first reference per booking.
reason: The recurring block is now inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, so it repeats per reference and still uses `updBooking.references.find`, deleting only one calendar event per booking.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The dynamic-user query no longer selects organization.
reason: Nothing in packages/features/bookings reads user.organization, and getBookerUrl (packages/lib/server/getBookerUrl.ts:4) takes only organizationId, so removing the selection has no effect.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The new try/catch turns errors into generic HTTP errors and exposes Prisma messages.
reason: Lines 757-761 turn the plain Error for an empty dynamic user list into a 500 and return raw Prisma error messages to the client as a 400.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: The caching tests were deleted instead of updated.
reason: The test removal was deliberate (commit 4472efe "clean up tests"); losing coverage of a simple cache is a remark, and nothing breaks.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: getBaseConditions can return a top-level OR without outer parentheses.
reason: A search finds no caller of getBaseConditions outside the test, which uses it alone as `WHERE ${baseConditions}`, so no query appends a predicate and the precedence problem cannot happen yet.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: The looser constructor type drops compile-time checking of options.
reason: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions was added on purpose and is checked at runtime by the zod safeParse; the constructor is only called from tests, so this is a typing preference, not a defect.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: findMany was removed from the public API.
reason: A repository search for InsightsBookingService finds only the service file and its integration test, so no caller of findMany is left to break.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: Rescheduling cancels at SendGrid right away instead of using the deferred cron path.
reason: EventManager.reschedule deletes the original booking (EventManager.ts:290) and the reminder rows go with it (onDelete: Cascade, schema.prisma:637), so a cancelled flag would never reach the cron; cancelling right away is deliberate (commit 'cancel rescheduled bookings immediately') and the suggested fix would break cancellation.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: Reminders cancelled shortly before their send time are still sent.
reason: The cron only cancels flagged reminders due within the next hour on each 15-minute run, so a reminder flagged after the last run and due before the next one is never cancelled at SendGrid and is still sent.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: One failed SendGrid cancel stops the whole batch, and no deletes run.
reason: All cancels share one try block (lines 53-77) and the delete calls only run when awaited by Promise.all after the loop, so one failed cancel skips every later cancel and every delete, and the same failing reminder blocks the batch on each run.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: Deleting a workflow or step still cancels immediately, so it still hits the 100-cancellation limit.
reason: Cancelling right away is required here because the step/workflow delete removes the reminder rows with it (schema.prisma:643); whether SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit can still be hit depends on live SendGrid state that can't be checked from the code.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: The override range check accepts slots that only partly overlap the override.
reason: Lines 117-125 reject only slots ending at/before override start or starting after override end, so partially overlapping slots pass and then hit the early `return true`.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: Slots inside a date override skip the busy-time check.
reason: Line 133-135 `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` returns before `busy.every(...)` at line 153, so busy times are never checked on override days.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: The working-hours check wrongly rejects slots for split schedules and ignores the slot's end.
reason: `workingHours.find` at 139-147 flags unavailable if any same-day entry doesn't contain the slot (breaks split schedules), and `end` at line 142 is computed from slotStartTime, so the slot's end time is never checked; the user's workingHours do reach this check via `...schedule`.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: Two dayjs objects are compared with ===, so the result is always false.
reason: Line 114 compares two freshly created dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so a start==end (unavailable) override does not reject a slot starting exactly at start.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: Shifted overrides can wrap past midnight or land on a different invitee day.
reason: Lines 218-223 reduce shifted instants to minutes-of-day, so a shift across midnight yields endTime < startTime, and activeOverrides is still chosen by the original UTC date at line 207.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: The override day is matched in server-local time and by UTC date, not the organizer's day.
reason: Lines 109-112 match the override day by the shifted override's UTC (or server-local) date against slotStartTime's UTC date, so an organizer-local override that falls on another UTC date marks the wrong UTC day as an override day.

head: 5f8a130277dbddc95d133cd2832be639baf89213
title: Match statistics are rolled back whenever the block actually happens.
reason: EmailValidator line 13 calls BlockedEmail.should_block? during User validation, and UsersController#create calls `user.save` (line 172), which runs validation inside a transaction and rolls it back when save returns false, so the match_count/last_match_at update is undone for blocked emails.

head: 5f8a130277dbddc95d133cd2832be639baf89213
title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so changing letter case gets past the block.
reason: EmailValidator passes the raw `value` to `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` and nothing downcases it first (User only validates email, and Email.downcase only lowercases the domain), so a different letter case gets past the block.

head: 5f8a130277dbddc95d133cd2832be639baf89213
title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses increments under concurrency.
reason: Lines 14-16 read the count, add one in Ruby and save it back with no lock or atomic update, so two signups at the same time can lose an increment; it is a small but real race.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Migration crashes when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id has no row in site_settings.
reason: Line 9-11 indexes [0] on a PG result that is empty when embed_category was never set; PG::Result#[] raises on an out-of-range index, aborting the migration.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Migrated hosts are not normalized or escaped, so existing embeds break, and the old settings are deleted anyway.
reason: Line 25 inserts each raw split line unquoted and unnormalized (bypassing the model's before_validation), then line 31 irreversibly deletes the source settings.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Every `*_ids` attribute on any REST model is now replaced, and a null value crashes hydration.
reason: Only rest_serializer endpoints are embedding, embeddable_hosts, queued_posts and similar_topics; none besides embedding serializes an `_ids` key, and embeddable_host_ids is always an array, so the described breakage has no trigger.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: update and destroy return a 500 for an unknown id.
reason: Lines 10 and 15 use where(...).first which returns nil for a missing id, so save_host(nil)/host.destroy raise NoMethodError → 500.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil.
reason: Lines 6-7 call sub! on self.host with no nil guard, so a request without host raises NoMethodError before validation.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Hosts saved with a port or uppercase letters never match.
reason: Validation permits `:port` and before_validation doesn't strip it, while record_for_host compares against uri.host (no port) without downcasing the input.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable host is configured.
reason: Removing the site-setting guard is an intentional consequence of moving hosts to a table; a topic with a TopicEmbed was already truncated, so this is a design choice rather than a defect.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: A delete failure is silently ignored.
reason: Line 46-48 destroyRecord().then(...) has no .catch(popupAjaxError), unlike save at line 40, so delete failures are silently swallowed.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Fabricator definitions are swapped between files.
reason: File placement of fabricators is an organizational/style remark; the finding itself notes everything works since all fabricators are loaded.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: Light and dark lightness values are swapped, so the light theme changes from 30% to 70%.
reason: dark-light-choose takes the light value first (variables.scss:46), so line 291 changes the light theme from the old 30% to 70%; the light and dark values are swapped.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: The light-theme color for `.group-member-info .name` changes from 30% to 50%.
reason: The old rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), but line 522's light branch (the first argument of dark-light-choose) is now 50%, which changes light-theme rendering.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: The values for `.custom-message-length` are inverted, so the hint becomes much darker on light themes.
reason: The old rule was 70%, but line 102's light branch is now 30% and its dark branch 70%, so the values are inverted from the pattern used elsewhere.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: The light-theme color for the topic map `h3` on mobile changes from 20% to 50%.
reason: The old h3 color was 20%, but line 182's light branch is now 50%, while the .number rule in the same file keeps (20%, 80%).

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: The light-theme color for `.group-member-info .name` on mobile changes from 30% to 50%.
reason: The old rule was 30%, but line 497's light branch is now 50%, which changes the light theme.

head: 5b229316ee4c661836ed1161139692a3e8527444
title: Making `.small-action` a flex container stops its `float: right` button from aligning right.
reason: small-action.hbs lines 5/8 put the buttons inside .small-action-desc, which is now a non-growing flex item sized to its content, so the button's float:right lands next to the text instead of at the post's right edge; the regression holds even though the 'float ignored on flex items' explanation is wrong, and the flex:1 fix is the right one.

head: ecfa17b5a79dfdc91e7a4d50b42ae78a35d0a293
title: The fallback chain depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the translate cache key doesn't include it.
reason: The cache key on line 72 of translate_accelerator.rb is built only from key, locale and backend, but the fallback chain on line 17 of i18n.rb reads SiteSetting.default_locale at runtime, and a repo search found no code that clears @cache or calls I18n.reload! when default_locale changes.

head: ecfa17b5a79dfdc91e7a4d50b42ae78a35d0a293
title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller, so translations outside a request don't fall back.
reason: translate (line 68) loads only config.locale, and the only call to I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is in application_controller.rb:159, so jobs/base.rb:151 and the db.rake tasks set I18n.locale and translate without loading :en or the default locale as fallbacks.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as read-only.
reason: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities with hardcoded `const isFederated = false` (line 245), so federated rules lose their read-only status.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: Grafana recording rules lose Pause, Restore, Export and DeletePermanently in the new list view.
reason: Lines 324-329 gate ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule, and GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule (line 47), so Grafana recording rules lose at least Export in the list view where the ruler check used to include them.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The `key` prop was dropped from list items rendered inside `rules.map`.
reason: FilterView.tsx line 157 renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> inside rules.map without key={key}, which the replaced GrafanaRuleLoader had.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The prom-based Pause and Delete abilities appear unused in the list view.
reason: The menu renders Pause only when rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) (line 123) and Delete only when `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165), and GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule, so the prom fallback for these two actions never shows anything in the list view.

head: 303cdc2caf256aa5df660611120c2e3f7392365d
title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new logger, so logs written through it are never recorded.
reason: No test asserts on logs written via TestLogger.FromContext (NewTestLogger users are installer/pipeline/process/store tests, none touch LoggerMiddleware), and returning a fresh logger mirrors the existing New() at line 19, so the fake's behavior causes no actual failure.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: Leftover debug logging at Error level dumps every batch's ID list
reason: Lines 534/537, 554/557 and 576/579 call r.log.Error on every batch, including the final empty one of a successful run, and the first of each pair logs the full ids slice plus an always-nil err; these are debug leftovers that produce false errors.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: Cleanup interval for all jobs cut from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which the request does not ask for
reason: Line 77 changes the ticker for every cleanup job from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no justification in the commits or the author's description, and the 9-minute per-run timeout at line 89 was sized for the old interval.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: Building the inline ID list with repeated Sprintf takes quadratic time
reason: Lines 609-612 rebuild the string with fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) for each ID, which is quadratic for large SQLite batches; this is a real performance defect even though the trigger is narrow.

head: b1613e320acff00623e6efc59f00ee68c7684a97
title: Cache is not re-checked after taking the write lock, so concurrent misses each reload the assets.
reason: Lines 41-49 read the cache under RLock, release it, then take Lock and reload without checking the cache again, so goroutines that missed at the same time each re-read and re-parse the manifest after the first one has filled the cache. That is real duplicated work, and the suggested re-check after Lock() fixes it.

head: 26fed312840cd76b766cbd2158e17a7e6c0ec548
title: The storage-server integration test is now skipped on Postgres instead of fixed.
reason: Commit 6f4d7087 'skips postgres integration test. Only fails in drone. Will fix later.' and the TODO show the author deliberately skipped it and explained why.

head: 26fed312840cd76b766cbd2158e17a7e6c0ec548
title: Removing per-request Init checks means a stopped server keeps serving requests.
reason: Stop (line 321) still sets s.initErr to reject new work, but the handlers no longer call s.Init (the only place that returned initErr), so after Stop they keep serving and IsHealthy stays healthy.

head: 26fed312840cd76b766cbd2158e17a7e6c0ec548
title: Narrower locking leaves cache readers such as TotalDocs racing with concurrent BuildIndex writes.
reason: TotalDocs' unlocked iteration (bleve.go:146) raced with map writes before this PR too, including the periodic call in bleve_index_metrics.go; init builds unique keys before the event goroutine starts (search.go:195-207), so the narrower lock doesn't introduce the race described.

head: e944e2acf1e64421860a8e827f93ad06c169621b
title: Cleanup removes the literal alias "alias" instead of the IDPs the test creates.
reason: Lines 381 and 425 register cleanup for get("alias")::remove, a provider that is never created, so the idp-alias-* providers created by the test are never cleaned up.

head: e944e2acf1e64421860a8e827f93ad06c169621b
title: The update check compares a wrapped model with the raw updated model, so the login cache can go stale.
reason: At line 441 the wrapper's isEnabled() returns false when the organization is disabled, and the login check uses IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled (IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:220), so a wrapped original can fail the check while the stored provider is in the cached login list, and an update that hides it skips invalidation.

head: 7355f05e6aafe2a7acc6434fb40c686665416606
title: canManage() lets callers with only the VIEW scope on groups manage them
reason: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() line 70 accepts VIEW, and its only caller GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (line 181 requireManage) lets a view-only admin create top-level groups, unlike canManage(GroupModel) and ClientPermissionsV2, which check MANAGE only.

head: 7355f05e6aafe2a7acc6434fb40c686665416606
title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs, not group IDs
reason: AdminPermissionsSchema names a group's resource after the group id (resolveGroup returns group.getId(), then resourceStore.create(server, name, ...)), so the hasPermission(groupResource.getId()) findByName lookup misses and the resource id, not the group id, is added to the set.

head: 7355f05e6aafe2a7acc6434fb40c686665416606
title: Group removal listener can call a V2 method that now throws
reason: Profile defines ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (version 1) and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (version 2) as versions of one feature, so only one can be on at a time; the listener is only registered under version 1, so it never reaches GroupPermissionsV2.

head: 1950a511026d520a7329c7b6b9ee60a4af8f8b55
title: V2 client permissions throw UnsupportedOperationException on paths that used to work
reason: TOKEN_EXCHANGE (v1) has no dependency on FGAP v1 in Profile.java, so with FGAP v2 enabled V1TokenExchangeProvider reaches AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo at AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276, which now throws UnsupportedOperationException (500) instead of allowing or denying; the management/permissions endpoint example is unreachable because it calls requireFeature(AD

head: 1950a511026d520a7329c7b6b9ee60a4af8f8b55
title: Test rotates the secret of the client the admin test client logs in with
reason: ManagedRealm uses the default per-class lifecycle (Supplier.getDefaultLifecycle returns LifeCycle.CLASS), so other FGAP classes get a fresh myclient with mysecret, and within this class the admin client's token is already obtained (line 200) before the rotation, so no later token fetch with the old secret happens in practice.

head: 4def149a50c4b9b2c24fbb753ac60fe4f4df0cac
title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can miss exceptions and the thread can loop forever.
reason: The thread started at lines 139-149 is never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can run before an in-flight request records its exception, and if a remove() on line 153 throws, deletedAll is never set and the reader loops forever.

head: 4def149a50c4b9b2c24fbb753ac60fe4f4df0cac
title: getSubGroupsCount can now return null, and a caller that unboxes it would throw an NPE.
reason: The only caller, GroupUtils.java:90, passes the result to GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(Long), which stores it in a Long field, so a null is never unboxed and cannot cause an NPE.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: isAccessTokenId never actually checks the grant shortcut
reason: Line 483 `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` gives "ta" for "onrtac" and returns false only on a match, so the matcher accepts any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` ID whatever the grant type.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories at startup
reason: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is in server-spi-private, which has no compatibility promise for extensions, and every built-in factory implements getShortcut(), so adding the method is intended.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: Null check for rawTokenId tests grantType instead
reason: Line 73 `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks the wrong argument, so the rawTokenId null check does nothing.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
reason: Nothing in the repo calls the removed copy constructor (the only `new OAuth2GrantType.Context(` is in TokenEndpoint:149 and always passes form params), and the class is private SPI.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: Every access token now needs session context client and a known grant shortcut
reason: getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) already ran during access-token creation through the access-token mappers, and every place that sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE (OAuth2GrantTypeBase, refresh, token exchange, pre-authorized code) uses a registered factory id, with null falling back to UNKNOWN, which has a registered shortcut.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: OptimizedCursorPaginator can't handle the datetime key used by audit logs.
reason: The audit log endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` at line 839 returns a datetime, and `math.floor`/`math.ceil` raise TypeError on it, unlike `DateTimePaginator` at lines 233-241, which converts first.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Negative cursor offsets are passed straight into a queryset slice.
reason: Line 880 passes a client-supplied negative `cursor.offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, and Django QuerySets reject negative indexing, so this branch can only end in a 500.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Switching from Redis sets to sorted sets breaks segment keys that already exist at deploy time.
reason: `buffer.py:197` now calls `p.zadd` on the same `span-buf:s:` key names that the old code wrote as SETs, and Redis returns WRONGTYPE for that until those keys expire.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Segments over 1000 spans are silently truncated during insert.
reason: The commit message for 74618671 says it deliberately "limits the number of spans per segment during insertion" and "evicts the oldest spans", so the truncation is the intended design.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: The "admin-only" gate trusts `has_global_access` and can dereference a missing member.
reason: Line 71 runs on every request, so a non-superuser whose `organization_context.member` is None (for example staff without membership) hits an AttributeError; and `has_global_access` defaults to True for ordinary members (`organizationmember.py:216`), so the gate does not restrict the path to admins.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Shared BasePaginator now passes negative offsets for prev cursors unchanged.
reason: Before this change both directions passed the raw `offset` to `queryset[offset:stop]`; the new line 182 only clamps the next-page direction, so the change does not make the prev-cursor case worse.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: The redirect-follow depth limit drops from 10000 to 1000 without explanation.
reason: This is the upstream eviction commit (#92393) and it changes the loop bound on purpose; the finding objects that the change is unexplained rather than showing a failure.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: ZUNIONSTORE sums the scores of duplicate members.
reason: `buffer.py:197` zadds each payload into the parent key, and the script then merges that key into `set_key` with zunionstore, whose default is AGGREGATE SUM; so a redelivered span already in `set_key` gets its score doubled, which breaks the eviction order.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: The consumer raises KeyError on spans without `end_timestamp_precise`.
reason: Whether a KeyError can happen depends on whether `end_timestamp_precise` is required in the external `sentry_kafka_schemas` `SpanEvent` schema, which is not in this repository.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: With the feature flag on, table widgets render an empty table and ignore the query results.
reason: The empty TableWidgetVisualization is gated behind the use-table-widget-visualization flag, and the commit says the table is not used yet with wiring coming in part 2, so this is an intentional stub.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Hidden attributes are only filtered out when a search term is entered.
reason: Lines 61-63 return `sorted` before the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter, so with the default empty search the hidden attributes are still shown.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Migrations 0917 and 0920 now do nothing and point to a 0921 migration that this PR does not add.
reason: src/sentry/migrations/0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py exists in the tree and defines convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Every paginated page gets all of the replay's errors.
reason: functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events) passes the full error list to every page, and gen_request_data yields all leftover errors, so each page includes every error of the replay.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Zipping error_ids with events.values() can pair an ID with the wrong event.
reason: nodestore get_multi (base.py:199-205) builds the dict from uncached items first and then adds cached items, so dict order can differ from id_list and the positional zip pairs IDs with the wrong events.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Error timestamps in seconds are compared with replay event timestamps in milliseconds.
reason: Nodestore event 'timestamp' is float seconds while rrweb recording events use epoch milliseconds, so the comparison at lines 153-155 is true for every error at the first event.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: This auth task deadline change and the saved-search migration rewrites aren't part of the replays bulk-delete request.
reason: This is a remark that the changes go beyond the PR description; it names no defect.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: The query cache key leaves out the organization, so different orgs can share cached attribute keys.
reason: The queryKey ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions] omits the organization while the queryFn uses organization.slug, and nothing clears the query cache on org switch.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Second placeholder group lost its gap and centring.
reason: The second placeholder group at line 27 is a bare <Flex> without the align/gap that the removed FlexBox provided.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: The detector owner is not checked against the detector's organization.
reason: ActorField.to_internal_value calls parse_and_validate_actor(data, self.context['organization'].id), which already checks the actor against the organization.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Tests no longer post with the real `application/reports+json` content type.
reason: TEST_REQUEST_DEFAULT_FORMAT is 'json' and the endpoint accepts JSONParser, so there is no 415 risk; what remains is a test-coverage remark.

head: 9501091c52ae94e8d916f79b35d21975b3f9cadb
title: `queued` default is set once at import time, not per instance.
reason: Line 18 `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain dataclass default, evaluated once when the class is defined, so every instance from `from_integration` carries the import-time timestamp rather than the time it was queued; `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` fixes it.

head: 9501091c52ae94e8d916f79b35d21975b3f9cadb
title: Task kwargs now carry a raw `datetime` that may not serialize.
reason: src/sentry/conf/server.py:739-741 sets CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle" and CELERY_ACCEPT_CONTENT = {"pickle"}, so the datetime in the task kwargs is pickled and comes back unchanged for `from_dict`.

head: dcdcadb771128e79259cc9eff9c70c38fc597976
title: Names moved out of mark_failed with no re-export can break existing importers
reason: A repo-wide search shows every importer of sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed (check_missed.py, check_timeout.py, monitor_consumer.py and two tests) imports only `mark_failed`, which still exists, and no test patches `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.*` or uses get_failure_reason, so nothing breaks.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: The factory builds one queue pool and shuts it down on the first rebalance, so every later message is dropped but still committed.
reason: The factory builds `queue_pool` once in `__init__` (lines 131-137) and every strategy shares it, but `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. After a rebalance, the new strategy's `put` raises `ShutDown`; `submit`'s `except` catches it and marks the offset complete, so the message is dropped and its offset committed.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: The queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure despite the docstring's claim.
reason: Each queue is created as `queue.Queue()` with no maxsize (line 185) and `submit` never raises `MessageRejected`, so the docstring's 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up' (line 253) does not happen and the queues can grow without limit.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: `close`/`join` stop the commit thread before the work is drained and never make a final commit.
reason: `close()` (lines 335-338) sets `shutdown_event` and joins the commit thread before `queue_pool.shutdown()`, and never makes a final commit, so work finished or still queued at close is not committed and gets redelivered.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: The arroyo `commit` callback is called from a background thread.
reason: `_commit_loop` runs on its own daemon thread and calls `commit_function` (line 287), which goes straight to arroyo's `Commit`. Arroyo expects commit from the processing thread, so this can race with the main loop and can commit partitions after they are revoked.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: The error-handling test asserts that nothing was committed, the opposite of its docstring, and depends on timing.
reason: Line 1922 asserts no commit for `test_partition` even though offsets 100 and 101 both complete, which contradicts the docstring. It passes only if the 1-second commit loop has not fired yet, so it depends on timing.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: A missing offset in a partition blocks commits for that partition forever.
reason: The contiguous scan at lines 89-93 does stall on a gap, but whether the uptime-results topic has gaps depends on how the external producer and broker are configured (transactions or compaction), and the repo's Kafka config shows neither.
